supporting_observations.claim: At 13:38:18, a network logon to WS-ICHEN-01 was recorded for sam.okafor from 10.40.10.23. At 13:39:45, PowerShell ran under sam.okafor with the documented Apply-Updates.ps1 path; it launched wusa to install a Windows update, and both processes exited shortly after 13:40.

The proxy recorded a successful tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com during that PowerShell activity, with approximately 38.8 MB returned. This is consistent with the stated workstation patching practice, but the logs do not establish that the update installed successfully.

At 13:28, Explorer wrote a UserAssist entry whose encoded executable path decodes to powershell.exe. This is evidence of a PowerShell-related UserAssist entry, not a process-creation record confirming the exact execution details.

At 14:08, after an interactive logon for ivy.chen, PowerShell ran with -Exec Bypass and the command line named C:\Scripts\cert-renewal.ps1. It created a temporary file and exited about 19 seconds later.

The 14:08 PowerShell activity is not explained by the supplied inventory or the documented patching practice. Its script name suggests a certificate-renewal purpose, but the available records do not establish what the script did or whether it was authorized.

An SMB connection to DC-NWD-01 occurred shortly after the 14:08 PowerShell start, but the recorded connection is attributed to System and does not establish that the PowerShell script initiated it or what data was accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show PowerShell command lines and a temporary-file creation, but not the contents, hash, signature, or behavior of C:\Scripts\cert-renewal.ps1 or the temporary file.
The records do not confirm whether the Windows update completed successfully.
The records do not establish whether ivy.chen saw the 13:39:45–13:40:02 PowerShell window; the reported timing is consistent with the recorded patching process.
The SMB record identifies System as the process, so it cannot be confidently attributed to the nearby PowerShell execution.
claims_not_established: That the PowerShell activity around 13:40 was malicious; the recorded command matches the documented patching path and timing.
That the 14:08 certificate-renewal script was malicious or authorized.
That the 14:08 PowerShell process caused the SMB connection or accessed sensitive data.
That the PowerShell activity at 13:28 represented a separate malicious execution.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve and review C:\Scripts\cert-renewal.ps1, including its hash, signature, file metadata, and source or deployment history.
Collect PowerShell script-block, module, and transcription logs for the 14:08 execution, if available.
Determine whether the certificate-renewal script is an approved or expected logon-time task for ivy.chen.
Review the SMB server-side share and file-access auditing around 14:08:20 to identify the share and objects accessed.
Verify the Windows update installation result and whether the patching run was authorized.
